title: Council
lede: How a hard decision gets pressure-tested by five advisors with clashing views, then turned into one committed recommendation.

ask.name: Owner asks
ask.role: The owner brings a high-stakes decision with real tradeoffs.
details: Triggers include "council this", "pressure-test this" or a real "should I X or Y" with stakes.

more: Factual lookups, yes/no questions, summaries and low-stakes advice skip the council.
If the question has a correct answer, the agent just answers it.

qs: When is a council worth the cost instead of just asking the agent once?

brief.name: Frame the brief
brief.role: The main agent writes a neutral, self-contained brief grounded in the repo.
details: States the decision, the options, the constraints and what success means.

more: Names the axes the decision balances, such as cost, speed, risk and reversibility.
Marks which options are beaten on every axis and which are genuine tradeoffs.

risks: A brief that tips toward one answer makes every advisor argue from the same slant.

advisors.name: Five advisors
advisors.role: Five isolated subagents each argue from one fixed lens, all at once.
details: 150 to 300 words each, no hedging, and no advisor sees another's answer.
They inherit the session's model; diversity comes from the persona, not the vendor.
risks: If isolated subagents are unavailable, the agent must say so and give a clearly labeled single-agent analysis instead.

head: Lens
Stance
rows: Assumes the plan breaks, and asks where and why.
Strips assumptions and asks whether this is even the right question.
Hunts hidden upside: what if this works better than expected?
Brings zero domain context and names what is confusing.
Cares only about implementation: what do you do Monday morning?

review.name: Peer review
review.role: Each advisor reviews all five answers with the authors hidden.
details: Answers are relabeled A to E in random order so reviewers judge the argument, not the persona.

more: Which response is strongest, and why?
Which has the biggest blind spot?

chair.name: Chairman verdict
chair.role: The main agent weighs the advisors and commits to one recommendation and a first step.
details: Weighs the advisors and never averages them.
Names real disagreement instead of papering it into false consensus.

more: Sections: where the council agrees, where it clashes, blind spots caught, the recommendation, the one thing to do first.
No files and no artifacts; the council edits nothing.

risks: "It depends" is not a verdict; the chairman has to commit.
qs: How does the chairman decide between two advisors who flatly disagree?

subagent.d: A separate agent run that cannot see the others.

trade.d: The axes a decision balances, such as cost, speed and risk.

chairman.d: The main agent, who writes the final verdict.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand scaffold's /council skill: how an AI agent pressure-tests a hard decision with five persona advisors.
